title: M/S Bharat Udyog Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. And Others
coram: Bharati Sapru, J. & Saral Srivastava, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed for non-prosecution; counsel holding brief had no instructions to prosecute
headnote: On 3 December 2012 a Division Bench recorded the consumer's challenge to U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. giving the FY 2012-13 tariff retrospective effect from 1 October 2012, though it was published in the newspaper only on 23 October 2012. Counsel relied on Clause 3.8(a) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, Section 24(7) of the U.P. Electricity Reforms Act, 1999, and Regulation 139(2) of the UPERC (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2004 — each providing that a published tariff takes effect only seven days after publication — and on Section 62(6) of the Electricity Act, 2003. The petitioner did not dispute the Commission's tariff determination. The Court held that the matter required consideration, issued notice (accepted for respondents 1 to 4), and stayed disconnection on the impugned bill on conditions: payment at the new tariff from 1 November 2012; payment at the prior tariff for October 2012 and of any pre-October amount in the bill by 10 December 2012; and a bank guarantee for the October difference by that date, without prejudice, with automatic vacation on default and with late-payment surcharge and interest recoverable if the writ failed. After listings, on 7 May 2018 counsel holding brief stated he had no instructions to prosecute. The writ was dismissed for non-prosecution, without a construction of Clause 3.8 or Section 24(7).
facts:
M/s Bharat Udyog Ltd. challenged an electricity bill that applied U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.'s new 2012-13 tariff from 1 October 2012, though the tariff was published in the newspaper only on 23 October 2012 (public notice, Annexure-3). The petitioner did not dispute the tariff as determined by the U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission, and challenged only the retrospective effect. Counsel invoked Clause 3.8(a) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, Section 24(7) of the U.P. Electricity Reforms Act, 1999, and Regulation 139(2) of the UPERC (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2004 — each said to make a published tariff effective only seven days after publication (31 October 2012) — and Section 62(6) of the Electricity Act, 2003 as a bar on recovering a tariff in excess of that determined under Section 62.

On 3 December 2012 notice was accepted for respondents 1 to 4, and disconnection on the impugned bill was stayed on conditions. After listings on 16 January 2013 and 10 July 2013, on 7 May 2018 counsel holding brief of the petitioner's advocate stated he had no instructions to prosecute; the writ was dismissed for non-prosecution.

holding_units.clause: 3.8(a) (tariff takes effect only after seven days from publication)
holding_units.topic: Interim stay of disconnection where a published tariff is given effect from a date before the seven-day publication window; writ later dismissed for non-prosecution
holding_units.question: Where a Commission-determined tariff is published on 23 October 2012, may the licensee apply it from 1 October 2012, or does Clause 3.8(a) confine its effect to seven days after publication?
holding_units.holding: Not decided on merits. The Court recorded the submission that publication on 23.10.2012 meant the new tariff could take effect only on 31.10.2012, held that the matter required consideration, issued notice (accepted for respondents 1 to 4), and as interim relief directed that supply would not be disconnected on the impugned bill if: (i) from 1.11.2012 the petitioner paid at the new tariff; (ii) for October 2012 it paid at the prior tariff by 10.12.2012; (iii) any pre-October amount in the bill was paid by that date; and (iv) the October difference was covered by a bank guarantee by that date, without prejudice. Default would vacate the stay automatically; if the writ were dismissed or the stay vacated, surcharge, interest and other late-payment charges would be recoverable from the guarantee and otherwise. The writ was later dismissed for non-prosecution without construing Clause 3.8.
holding_units.qualifier: Prima facie and interlocutory (3.12.2012, Satya Poot Mehrotra, J. and Het Singh Yadav, J.); the petition was dismissed for non-prosecution on 7.5.2018 (Bharati Sapru, J. and Saral Srivastava, J.).

holding_units.clause: 24(7) (tariff comes into force after seven days from the last date of publication)
holding_units.topic: Section 24(7) seven-day publication rule invoked with Clause 3.8(a); not finally construed
holding_units.holding: The petitioner submitted that Section 24(7) required the new tariff to come into force only after seven days from the last date of publication (23.10.2012), so it could not be given retrospective effect from 1.10.2012. The Court recorded the submission, held that the matter required consideration, and moulded interim billing accordingly. It did not finally construe Section 24(7).

holding_units.code: Article 226 — dismissal for want of prosecution
holding_units.topic: Writ dismissed for non-prosecution when counsel holding brief had no instructions
holding_units.holding: On 7.5.2018 counsel holding brief of the petitioner's advocate stated he had no instructions to prosecute the matter. The writ was dismissed for non-prosecution, without a final ruling on the retrospective-tariff bill. The 3.12.2012 interim order had already provided that, on dismissal of the writ, the petitioner would be liable for surcharge, interest and other late-payment charges, recoverable from the bank guarantee and otherwise.

principle_tags.application: Prima facie, and only as an interim billing arrangement, a tariff published on 23.10.2012 was not applied from 1.10.2012: the petitioner was to pay at the new rate from 1.11.2012 and at the prior rate for October, with a bank guarantee for the October difference. Clause 3.8(a) and Section 24(7) were not finally construed.

Disconnection on the impugned bill was stayed pending notice, subject to payment of the new tariff from 1.11.2012, payment at the prior tariff for October 2012 and of pre-October amounts by 10.12.2012, and a bank guarantee for the October difference, without prejudice and self-vacating on default.

Counsel holding brief having no instructions to prosecute, the writ was dismissed for non-prosecution on 7.5.2018; the 3.12.2012 order already made the petitioner liable for late-payment surcharge and interest on dismissal. The Clause 3.8 / Section 24(7) challenge was left unadjudicated.

not_decided.point: Whether the FY 2012-13 tariff published on 23.10.2012 could lawfully be given effect from 1.10.2012, or only from 31.10.2012 under Clause 3.8(a), Section 24(7) and Regulation 139(2)
not_decided.note: The 3.12.2012 view was that the matter required consideration; dismissal for non-prosecution left the effective date unadjudicated.

not_decided.point: Whether Section 62(6) of the Electricity Act, 2003 independently barred recovery of the new tariff for October 2012
not_decided.note: Cited by the petitioner as a bar on recovering tariff in excess of that determined under Section 62; not applied. EA2003::62 is not a catalog key.

not_decided.point: Validity of the new tariff as determined by the U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission
not_decided.note: The petitioner expressly did not dispute the Commission's determination.
